clue.text: Eastern type of beam brought over for onward disposal

indicators.note: brought over means the whole run of pieces is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a laser produces a narrow beam of light

explanation.surface: Instructions for shipping off some imported girder for disposal elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns the whole of E + LASER round, giving the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling something on to a further buyer is a second sale, an onward disposal of goods.

clue.text: Note idiot man put new garment on

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a clot is a fool, an idiot
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a foolish fellow has changed into fresh clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone again in fresh clothing is to put a new garment on them.

clue.text: Used tool to move earth from winter transport outside shack

indicators.note: outside means the sledge's letters go round the shack's

parts.note: a sled carries people over snow in winter
a hovel is a wretched little shack

explanation.surface: A gardener dug soil away from a hut that has a sledge parked round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the sledge word around the shack word; 'from' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting soil with a spade-like implement is the action of digging with that tool, past tense.

clue.text: Used wrong words in German song

explanation.surface: A singer fluffed the words of a German art song.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking falsehoods is telling untruths; and a Lied is a German art song, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Moose returns, after short season, for water

indicators.note: after means the moose piece is placed behind the season piece
short means the season word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: returns means the moose word is read backwards

parts.note: elk is another name for the moose

explanation.surface: A moose comes back after a brief spring to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the season's last letter, 'returns' turns the moose backwards, and 'after' sets it behind. 'water' is a verb, as in watering a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To water plants is to scatter drops over them, as a gardener does with a can.

clue.text: Get in first before temp goes wrong

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: goes wrong means the letters of temp are scrambled

explanation.surface: Getting in ahead of a temporary worker who has made a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges the four letters of temp; the answer is written with a hyphen, pre-empt.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall someone is to act ahead of them, beating them to it.

clue.text: This article could be an unknown

explanation.surface: An editor muses that a piece might be by an anonymous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'a' or 'an' the indefinite article; and something vague or not yet fixed is indefinite.

clue.text: King joining poor Ivor in Russian ballet

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: poor means the letters of Ivor are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A king teams up with a struggling Ivor at a Russian ballet company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of Ivor, placed after the king's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kirov is the famous St Petersburg ballet company, now called the Mariinsky.

clue.text: In Aberdeen Corelli provides material for further performance

indicators.note: In means the letters lie inside the words Aberdeen Corelli, across the join

explanation.surface: A Scottish concert of Corelli's music gives the audience something to clap for again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'AberdeEN CORElli'; 'provides material for' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra piece played at the audience's call after a concert ends is an additional performance.

clue.text: Brown takes first-class wife in eastern island

indicators.note: takes means the brown word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
A1 (written AI) means first-class

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown brings a splendid wife on a trip to an Asian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' puts the first-class mark and the wife inside the colour word. A1 is the classic first-class rating, read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the coast of China in East Asia.

clue.text: Vat man and Greek character about to work together

parts.note: a cooper makes barrels and vats

indicators.note: about means the Greek letter's name is turned round

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A barrel maker and a Greek fellow are about to join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the Greek letter round. It looks like part of 'about to', a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate is to act jointly with others toward a shared goal.

clue.text: Gold-lined cube almost in classical style

indicators.note: Gold-lined says the gold piece forms a lining inside the cube piece
almost means the last letter of the cube word is dropped

parts.note: a dice is a small cube used in games
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A small cube with a gold lining, in an old-fashioned style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from the cube word, and 'lined' puts the heraldic gold inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the plainest of the Greek orders of architecture, a classical style of column.

clue.text: Sign cryptically indicating females only?

parts.note: a portent, whose letters split as a nought followed by males, that is, no males present, leaving only the fair sex

explanation.surface: A notice that reads like a women-only sign on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as O (nought) followed by a word for males: 'no males', so females only; the whole means a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent of what is to come is a sign, good or bad.

clue.text: Overwhelm fellow, always a danger to Arabs?

parts.note: to swamp is to overwhelm
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A threatening man who forever poses a risk to Middle Eastern people.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are the horse breed, not people: swamp fever is an infectious disease of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine infectious anaemia, a disease of horses, threatens Arab horses among others.

clue.text: Put back, say, a support for the seventies?

indicators.note: Put back means the abbreviation for say and the a are read backwards together

parts.note: e.g. means for example, that is, say
a bracket is a support fixed to a wall

explanation.surface: Instructions to replace a shelf support in a seventies room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns 'say' and 'a' round together; 'the seventies' is people aged seventy to seventy-nine, not the decade.
explanation.definitionFit: People aged from seventy to seventy-nine form one band of years, a grouping by how old they are.

clue.text: Ring to get information on iodine or bromine?

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Phoning to get facts about two chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is a circle of light; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine and bromine are both examples of the halogen group of elements, alongside fluorine and chlorine.

clue.text: Large fish swallows doctor in northern region

indicators.note: swallows means the fish word takes the doctor inside it

parts.note: a tuna is a large ocean fish

explanation.surface: A big fish gulps down a physician in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts the doctor's abbreviation inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeless Arctic plain of northern Russia and Canada is a cold northern zone.

clue.text: Lying about copper and doctor at hospital department

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Someone is telling lies about a policeman and a doctor in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths, but means lying down; 'copper' is the metal, not the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclining flat, as a figure on a tomb does, is being in a lying position.

clue.text: Dilatory, dissembling cleverly

indicators.note: dissembling, taking apart the assembly, means the letters of dilatory are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone slow and deceitful, yet clever about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissembling' rearranges the letters of DILATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something skilfully and with quick cleverness is doing it deftly.

clue.text: Apt to be taken in by lie deb spun

indicators.note: spun means the letters of lie deb are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fit to be fooled by a debutante's spun lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like deceived, but here means eaten; 'spun' rearranges LIE DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Food fit to be eaten is safe to consume, suitable to be taken into the body.

clue.text: Girl all set to change after marriage at last

indicators.note: after means the rearranged piece follows the letter from marriage
at last picks the final letter of marriage
to change means the letters of all set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl is all prepared for a new life once she is finally married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges ALL SET into STELLA, placed 'after' E, the last letter of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is a female name, the cold heroine of Dickens's Great Expectations.

clue.text: Unfortunately can't help about an indigestion remedy

indicators.note: about means the help word goes round the other piece

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: Unfortunately means the letters of can't are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, nothing can be done to relieve an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges the letters of can't, and 'about' wraps the word for help around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet that neutralises stomach acid is a common remedy for heartburn.

clue.text: Make reference to Lord in drink

indicators.note: in means the lord word goes inside the drink word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
lud is the old form of lord, as in 'm'lud' in court

explanation.surface: Mentioning a peer who is in his cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the lord word inside the drink. 'M'lud' is how British barristers address a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer indirectly to something is to mention it in passing, hinting at it.

clue.text: Method that's awfully messy, taking up time

indicators.note: taking up means the rearranged letters absorb the time piece
awfully means the letters of messy are scrambled

explanation.surface: An approach that is dreadfully untidy and wastes time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges MESSY into SYSEM, and 'taking up' puts T inside: SYS-T-EM.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised scheme or procedure for doing things is a method.

clue.text: Permission to speak which suggests one hasn't the moral high ground?

definitions.text: which suggests one hasn't the moral high ground?

explanation.surface: Someone is given the floor, and also told they are hardly the one to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Said literally, the phrase allows someone to have their say; said as a retort, it means the critic is equally guilty.

clue.text: A French charge for workers' organisation

parts.note: un is French for a
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A French fee charged to a body of labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee, but means an electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is a body that represents employees in dealing with employers.

clue.text: Doctor on morning rounds

indicators.note: on means the doctor piece is placed after the morning piece in this across clue

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A GP doing ward visits first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like a doctor's visits, but means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is counted in rounds, each one a single cartridge for a gun.

clue.text: Flying in Faeroes

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the word Faeroes

explanation.surface: An air trip to the Faeroe Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'fAEROes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aero- is the prefix for flight and aircraft, as in aeronautics, so relating to flying.

clue.text: Cheat at cards?

explanation.surface: A card sharp is accused of dishonest play.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone is to deceive them; and in card games each round of play won is a trick.

clue.text: Money deposited in Masons' account finally?

parts.note: Freemasons meet in a lodge, so they are lodge men

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of account

explanation.surface: Cash paid into the Freemasons' bank account at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasons belong to a lodge, so they are lodge men; 'finally' adds T, the last letter of account.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit of cash, as paid into a bank, is a sum lodged there.

clue.text: Current article goes into tiny details

indicators.note: goes into means the current and article pieces are put inside the tiny word

parts.note: minute means extremely small
I is the symbol for electric current
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An up-to-date piece of writing explores small particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' puts I and A inside MINUTE: MINUT-IA-E. 'Current' looks like up-to-date, but is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are small, precise points, the fine particulars of something.

clue.text: Dear greek island ends in almost total anarchy

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: ends in picks the last letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A beloved Greek island ends up almost in complete chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends in' takes T, L and Y, the last letters of almost, total and anarchy, after COS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear has a high price, so it is expensive.
